prompt:
The museum first opened its doors in \_\_\_\_\_\_ now holds more than 4,000 paintings.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

prompt:
Some hummingbirds can beat their wings up to 80 times per \_\_\_\_\_\_ speed allows them to hover in place while they feed.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: “This speed allows them to hover…” is a complete sentence, so it needs its own sentence (or a semicolon). In “second, and this,” the comma after “this” wrongly splits the subject from its noun.

prompt:
The engineers tested the bridge model in a wind \_\_\_\_\_\_ results were better than expected.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: A comma plus “and” correctly joins two complete sentences. A semicolon shouldn’t be followed by “and”, and in “tunnel and, the” the comma is misplaced.

prompt:
Solar panels can lower electricity bills over \_\_\_\_\_\_ the upfront cost of installing them remains too high for many households.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

prompt:
Ada Lovelace wrote what many historians consider the first computer \_\_\_\_\_\_ 1843, she described how a mechanical engine could calculate a series of numbers.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The second sentence explains the first, so a colon fits after the complete first sentence. A comma creates a comma splice.

prompt:
The violin’s body is carved from spruce and \_\_\_\_\_\_ woods prized for the way they carry sound.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: “Woods prized for…” isn’t a complete sentence; it describes spruce and maple. A comma attaches it. A semicolon or period would leave a fragment.

prompt:
The expedition packed three essentials for the \_\_\_\_\_\_ water filters, solar chargers, and a satellite phone.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

prompt:
The museum’s newest \_\_\_\_\_\_ a 2,000-year-old bronze mirror — arrived from Athens last week.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The phrase about the mirror is closed by a dash, so it must be opened by a dash too.

prompt:
The tour stopped in Lagos, \_\_\_\_\_\_ Accra, Ghana; and Dakar, Senegal.

prompt:

prompt:
The chef’s famous stew uses only one unusual \_\_\_\_\_\_ smoked paprika.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

prompt:
Mount Kilimanjaro — the tallest mountain in \_\_\_\_\_\_ rises about 5,895 meters above sea level.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

prompt:
The Amazon River, which carries more water than any other river in the \_\_\_\_\_\_ empties into the Atlantic Ocean.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: “Mathematician” is a title that identifies her, so no commas surround the name.

prompt:

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

prompt:

After three years of \_\_\_\_\_\_ engineers finally launched the weather satellite.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

The bridge \_\_\_\_\_\_ in 1937 is still one of the longest suspension bridges in the country.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: “That opened in 1937” identifies which bridge, so it takes no commas. “, which opened” would need a closing comma before “is”.

prompt:
The list of approved projects \_\_\_\_\_\_ posted on the main board every Friday.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The subject is “list” (singular), not “projects”.

prompt:
Each of the twelve paintings in the exhibit \_\_\_\_\_\_ by a different artist.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: “Each” is singular, so it takes the singular verb “was”.

prompt:
The research team’s findings about the coral \_\_\_\_\_\_ surprising to many marine biologists.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The subject is “findings” (plural), so the verb is “were”.

prompt:
The orchestra \_\_\_\_\_\_ preparing for its first international tour.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: “Orchestra” acts as a single group here (“its” tour), so it takes the singular verb.

prompt:
Rainfall and temperature \_\_\_\_\_\_ when the hillside flowers bloom each spring.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: Two subjects joined by “and” are plural, so the verb is “determine”.

Among the artifacts in the glass display case \_\_\_\_\_\_ a small bronze key that may have opened the temple’s main door.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The sentence is inverted: the subject is “a small bronze key” (singular), which comes after the verb.

prompt:
After years of research, the startup finally unveiled \_\_\_\_\_\_ first electric tractor.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: A startup is a single company, so the possessive is “its”. “It’s” means “it is”.

The \_\_\_\_\_\_ nests were found high on the cliffs above the bay.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: Several falcons own the nests, so the plural possessive “falcons’” is needed.

prompt:
When visitors enter the cave, \_\_\_\_\_\_ must wear a helmet at all times.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The pronoun refers to “visitors”, which is plural, so “they” is right. Switching to “one” or “you” changes the point of view.

prompt:
A tortoise can pull \_\_\_\_\_\_ head completely inside its shell when it feels threatened.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The head belongs to the tortoise, so the possessive “its” (no apostrophe) is right.

prompt:
The volunteers, \_\_\_\_\_\_ had trained for months, finished the mountain trail in record time.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The pronoun refers to people and acts as the subject of “had trained”, so “who” is right.

prompt:
The \_\_\_\_\_\_ final letter, written just weeks before her death, was discovered in an attic in 2015.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: One poet (“her death”) owns the letter, so the singular possessive “poet’s” is needed.

prompt:
By the time the firefighters arrived, the flames \_\_\_\_\_\_ to the second floor of the warehouse.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The spreading happened before another past event (the arrival), so the past perfect “had spread” is right.

prompt:
In 1969, astronauts \_\_\_\_\_\_ on the Moon for the first time, an event watched by hundreds of millions of people.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: “In 1969” is a specific past time, so the simple past “walked” is right.

Built in the twelfth century, \_\_\_\_\_\_

the castle still attracts thousands of tourists every summer.
every summer thousands of tourists visit the castle.
visiting the castle remains popular with tourists.

The program teaches students to design experiments, to collect data, and \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: Items in a list should match: “to design… to collect… to analyze”.

Exhausted after the eight-hour climb, \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the summit was where the hikers finally rested.
the hikers finally rested at the summit.
resting at the summit was a relief for the hikers.
a rest at the summit was taken by the hikers.

prompt:
The swimmer had \_\_\_\_\_\_ the channel twice before she turned twenty.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: After “had”, use the past participle. For “swim” it’s “swum” (swim, swam, swum).

prompt:
Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they support about a quarter of all known marine species. Because of this outsized role, marine biologists describe reefs as \_\_\_\_\_\_ to ocean biodiversity.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: Reefs support a huge share of species from a tiny area, so they are **essential** to biodiversity. “Incidental” means the opposite; “opposed” and “identical” don’t fit the logic.

prompt:
Many early films had no recorded sound. To help audiences follow the story, filmmakers \_\_\_\_\_\_ short written cards, called intertitles, between scenes.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: The cards appear **between scenes** to help viewers, so filmmakers **inserted** them. “Removed” and “avoided” contradict the text.

prompt:
Although the trail looked \_\_\_\_\_\_ on the map, hikers found it steep and rocky, with several difficult climbs.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: “Although” signals a contrast with “steep and rocky”, so the trail must have looked **easy**. “Challenging” and “dangerous” agree with the second half instead of contrasting with it.

prompt:
The town council voted to \_\_\_\_\_\_ the old library rather than demolish it, restoring its original windows and repairing its roof.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: “Rather than demolish it” and the restoration work show that the council chose to **preserve** the building.

prompt:
The baker’s new recipe was an \_\_\_\_\_\_ success: within a week of its launch, customers were lining up around the block.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: Lines formed **within a week**, so the success was **immediate**. “Eventual” suggests a long wait, and “uncertain” contradicts the lines of customers.

prompt:
In her memoir, the architect recalls that her early designs were often dismissed as impractical. Yet she remained \_\_\_\_\_\_, submitting proposal after proposal until a city finally commissioned one of her buildings.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: She kept “submitting proposal after proposal” despite rejection, which shows she was **persistent**.

prompt:
The committee’s report was **sound**: every recommendation rested on careful analysis of the evidence.

As used in the text, what does the word “sound” most nearly mean?
explain: The report is described as resting on careful analysis, so “sound” means **well-founded** or reliable. “Noisy” is a different meaning of the word.

prompt:
Researchers had assumed that the warbler’s long migration was guided mainly by the position of the sun. New tracking data \_\_\_\_\_\_ that view: birds flying under thick cloud cover stayed on course just as accurately as birds flying under clear skies.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: If birds navigate just as well when they can’t see the sun, the data **challenge** the idea that the sun is their main guide.

prompt:
The novelist is known for her \_\_\_\_\_\_ prose: she rarely uses two words where one will do.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: Using as few words as possible is the definition of **concise** writing. “Ornate” means the opposite.

prompt:
When it opens next spring, the museum’s new wing will **house** a collection of more than 3,000 photographs.

As used in the text, what does the word “house” most nearly mean?
explain: The wing will hold the photographs, so “house” means **contain**. A wing can’t “live in” a collection.

prompt:
Some historians have portrayed the inventor as a lone genius. Letters recently found in an archive, however, reveal that her breakthroughs were often \_\_\_\_\_\_ efforts, shaped by daily exchanges with a circle of fellow engineers.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: “However” contrasts the lone-genius image with work “shaped by daily exchanges” with others, so the efforts were **collaborative**. “Solitary” repeats the view being rejected.

prompt:
Although the musician’s first albums sold poorly, critics now regard them as \_\_\_\_\_\_: techniques she pioneered on those records appear in the work of dozens of later artists.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: Her techniques show up in many later artists’ work, so the albums were **influential**. “Derivative” and “conventional” suggest she copied others, the reverse of pioneering.

prompt:
The study’s authors are careful not to overstate their results. They describe the link they observed between sleep and memory as \_\_\_\_\_\_ rather than definitive, noting that their sample included only forty participants.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: The authors avoid overstating and contrast the word with “definitive”, so the link is **tentative**. “Conclusive” means the same as “definitive”.

prompt:
Marine scientists warn that even a small rise in water temperature could **compromise** the reef’s ability to recover after major storms.

As used in the text, what does the word “compromise” most nearly mean?
explain: A temperature rise would harm the reef’s ability to recover, so “compromise” means **weaken** here, not “settle” or “agree to”.

prompt:
The documentary does not simply celebrate the expedition; it also \_\_\_\_\_\_ its costs, describing the injuries and debts that team members carried for years afterward.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: “Not simply celebrate… it also” means the film adds an honest look at the downside: it **acknowledges** the costs. Nothing suggests it exaggerates or invents them.

prompt:
Honeybees perform a “waggle dance” to tell other bees in the hive where to find flowers. ==The angle of the dance shows the direction of the flowers relative to the sun.== The length of the waggle portion shows how far away the flowers are.

options: It explains one way the dance communicates the location of food.
It introduces a debate about how bees choose flowers.
It provides evidence that bees cannot see certain colors.
It describes how bees build the cells of the hive.

options: It describes a problem and then proposes several solutions to it.
It presents an earlier belief and then describes evidence that challenged it.
It compares the hunting methods of two species of squid.
It explains how deep-sea cameras are built and used.

prompt:

To explain how rain forms over deserts
To show that the Sonoran Desert supports a variety of life adapted to dry conditions
To compare the plants of deserts with those of rain forests

prompt:
The poet Lena Morales spent her first two collections describing the noise and crowds of the city where she grew up. ==A summer spent on her grandmother’s farm in 1998 changed that.== Her later books are full of orchards, fields and the slow turning of seasons.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It gives an example of the city scenes in her early poems.
It criticizes the poems she wrote after 1998.
It describes her grandmother’s work as a farmer.
It identifies the event that marked a shift in the subjects of her poetry.
explain: The sentence sits between her city poems and her rural poems and explains what caused the change.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It offers evidence that bears on the disagreement described earlier in the text.
It explains why economists first became interested in wages.
It proves that raising the minimum wage always increases employment.
It describes a method for measuring staff turnover.
explain: The first two sentences describe a disagreement; the study provides evidence relevant to it. “Proves… always” is far too strong for one study.

prompt:

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

It argues that glass frogs are more closely related to fish than to other frogs.
It compares glass frogs with other animals that can change color.
It explains why scientists stopped studying glass frogs.
explain: The text sets up a puzzle (red blood should be visible) and then explains how the frogs hide it.

prompt:

To describe the history of Rosa’s neighborhood

options: It presents one side of the debate introduced in the first sentence.
It states the author’s final conclusion about skyscrapers.
It explains how concrete is manufactured.
It provides an example that supports the view of skyscrapers’ supporters.
explain: The first sentence introduces a debate; the underlined sentence gives the critics’ side, and the last sentence gives the supporters’ side.

prompt:

Many teachers assign homework every night, believing that regular practice outside class strengthens every student’s skills.

By suggesting that the belief may hold for older students but not for the youngest ones
By arguing that homework harms high school students
By claiming that no studies of homework have been done

prompt:

The new mural on Grant Street is a failure. Its images are so small and densely packed that, from across the street, it looks like a gray blur.

They would argue that the mural should be repainted with larger images.
They would suggest that the mural’s appeal comes from viewing it up close, which the claim in Text 1 overlooks.
They would claim that the mural is easy to see from across the street.
explain: Text 1 judges the mural from a distance; Text 2 says its value is in the small details seen up close.

prompt:
**Text 1**
Some linguists claim that languages spoken in isolated places change more slowly than other languages, since isolated speakers have little contact with other languages that could introduce new words and sounds.

**Text 2**
A study of languages on remote Pacific islands found that several had changed faster than related languages on the mainland. The researchers suggest that in very small communities, a new word or pronunciation can spread to everyone quickly.

Based on the texts, how would the researchers in Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1?
options: They would point out evidence that isolation does not always slow language change.
They would agree that isolated languages never change.
They would argue that mainland languages do not change at all.
They would claim that contact with other languages slows change.
explain: Text 2’s findings contradict the claim that isolation slows change, and offer a reason why small communities might change faster.

prompt:
**Text 1**
Community gardens give city residents access to fresh, affordable vegetables, which can be hard to find in some neighborhoods.

**Text 2**
Beyond producing food, city gardens can lower nearby summer temperatures, because plants and soil absorb less heat than pavement does.

Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?
options: Gardens are the only way to cool a city.
City gardens can offer benefits to residents.
Vegetables from gardens are more expensive than store-bought ones.
Pavement is better than soil for cities.
explain: Each text describes a different benefit (food in Text 1, cooler temperatures in Text 2), so both would agree gardens benefit residents.

prompt:
**Text 1**
Feathers are a key part of what makes flight possible for birds. Some researchers therefore assume that feathers first evolved because they helped the ancestors of birds fly.

**Text 2**
Fossils show that many dinosaurs had feathers yet clearly could not fly; some were far too large, and others had short, fuzzy feathers unsuited to flight. Feathers probably first helped animals stay warm or attract mates.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the assumption described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that feathers evolved mainly for flight
By arguing that feathers likely served other purposes before they were used for flight
By claiming that birds did not evolve from dinosaurs
By suggesting that feathered dinosaurs were excellent fliers
explain: Text 2 notes many feathered dinosaurs couldn’t fly and proposes warmth or display as the first functions.

prompt:
**Text 1**
In several experiments, students who read passages on screens answered fewer comprehension questions correctly than students who read the same passages on paper. Educators should therefore be cautious about replacing printed textbooks with digital ones.

**Text 2**

They would claim that paper reading is always better than screen reading.
They would agree that digital textbooks should never be used.
They would suggest that students read faster on screens.

prompt:
**Text 1**
The printing press, introduced in Europe in the 1450s, made books far cheaper. As a result, the historian Paul Arnaud argues, literacy spread rapidly among ordinary people within a few decades.

**Text 2**
Records of signatures in marriage registers suggest that literacy rates in much of Europe rose slowly for more than a century after printing arrived. Early printed books were bought mostly by people who could already read: clergy, scholars and merchants.

options: By agreeing that the press immediately made most people literate
By arguing that the printing press had no effect on literacy
By suggesting that the press’s effect on literacy was more gradual than Arnaud claims
By claiming that books became more expensive after the printing press
explain: Text 2 doesn’t deny the press mattered, but its evidence shows slow change, contradicting “rapidly… within a few decades”.

prompt:

Tariffs on imported steel protect jobs at home. When foreign steel becomes more expensive, buyers turn to domestic producers, who can then keep or hire more workers.

After a set of steel tariffs took effect, steel-making jobs rose slightly. But companies that use steel to make cars, appliances and machinery faced higher costs, and some cut jobs. Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the argument in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that tariffs increase total employment
By pointing out that tariffs may cost jobs in industries that buy steel
By claiming that steel-making jobs fell after the tariffs
By arguing that foreign steel is of lower quality
explain: Text 2 accepts the small gain in steel jobs but adds that steel-using industries lost jobs, which Text 1 ignores.

explain: Jumping spiders do the opposite of most spiders, so a contrast transition is needed.

prompt:

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: The closure caused commuters to switch, so a cause-and-effect transition fits.

prompt:

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: The crows are a specific example of animals using tools.

prompt:

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: The sentences describe steps in order, so a sequence transition fits.

prompt:
