Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: A shorter battery life is a drawback that contrasts with the improved screen.

prompt:
Scientists long believed that only humans use grammar, combining sounds in rule-governed orders to create meaning. \_\_\_\_\_\_ studies of a small Japanese songbird have shown that it responds differently to the same calls depending on the order in which they are arranged.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: The bird study goes against the older belief, so a contrast transition is needed.

prompt:
Organizers expected the town’s first jazz festival to draw about 5,000 visitors. \_\_\_\_\_\_ more than 12,000 people attended over the weekend.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: The attendance differs from the expectation, and “As it turned out” introduces what actually happened.

prompt:
An octopus has about 500 million neurons. \_\_\_\_\_\_ roughly two-thirds of those neurons are located not in its brain but in its eight arms.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: The second sentence adds a surprising fact about the first, and “Remarkably” signals that. “Therefore” would claim one fact causes the other.

prompt:
The first small trial of the new treatment produced promising results. \_\_\_\_\_\_ the researchers designed a larger study to test whether the results would hold up.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: The promising results led to the larger study, so a transition meaning “as a result” fits. “Nevertheless” and “Even so” mean the same thing as each other, a hint that neither is right.

prompt:
Spider silk is remarkably light: a strand long enough to circle Earth would weigh only a few hundred grams. \_\_\_\_\_\_ some types of spider silk are, for their weight, stronger than steel.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: Being light might suggest being weak; “Yet” introduces the surprising fact that it is very strong.

prompt:
The novelist’s first three books are set in the small Ohio town where she grew up. \_\_\_\_\_\_ her later novels range across the world, from the markets of Lagos to the trams of Lisbon.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: The later novels’ global settings differ from the early books’ single town, so a contrast transition fits.

prompt:
Sea otters often float on their backs while they eat. To open hard-shelled prey such as clams, an otter balances a rock on its chest and strikes the shell against it until it cracks. Some otters even keep a favorite rock tucked in a loose pouch of skin under a foreleg, carrying it from one meal to the next.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Sea otters prefer clams to every other kind of food.
Sea otters use rocks as tools to open shelled prey.
Sea otters spend most of their lives floating on their backs.
Sea otters store food in pouches of skin.
explain: Every sentence after the first is about using rocks to crack shells. The pouch holds a rock, not food.

prompt:
In 2019, the city of Ridgeport planted 400 trees along its main shopping street. City officials explained that the trees were meant to shade the sidewalks and lower summer temperatures, which had been rising for a decade. Shop owners later reported an unexpected benefit: more people strolled the street on hot afternoons.

According to the text, why did Ridgeport plant the trees?
options: To attract more shoppers to the street
To replace trees that had been damaged
To provide shade and reduce summer heat
explain: Officials said the trees were meant to shade sidewalks and lower temperatures. More shoppers was an **unexpected** benefit, not the reason.

prompt:
My grandfather never hurried. When my bicycle chain snapped, he spread a cloth on the garage floor and laid out each tool in a row. “Again,” he said quietly each time the new link slipped from my fingers. By the time the chain finally held, the afternoon was gone, and I realized I had stopped wanting to rush.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The narrator learns patience from her grandfather while they repair a bicycle.
The narrator’s grandfather is frustrated by the broken chain.
The narrator decides to buy a new bicycle.
The narrator’s grandfather teaches her how to organize a garage.
explain: The grandfather’s calm, step-by-step approach and the narrator’s final realization show that she learns patience.

prompt:
Tardigrades are tiny animals, less than a millimeter long, that can survive conditions that would kill most living things. When their surroundings dry out, they lose nearly all the water in their bodies and curl into a shape called a tun. In this state, they can wait for years until water returns, at which point they rehydrate and become active again.

According to the text, what happens when tardigrades form a tun?
options: They grow larger to store more water.
They lose most of the water in their bodies and curl up.
They search for a new source of water.
explain: The text says they “lose nearly all the water in their bodies and curl into a shape called a tun.”

prompt:
The ancient city of Petra, in present-day Jordan, sits in a dry, rocky landscape. Its builders carved many structures directly into the sandstone cliffs. To supply the city with water, they cut channels into the rock and built underground cisterns that captured the brief but heavy winter rains, storing enough water to support a population of thousands.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Petra’s builders were the first people to carve buildings out of rock.
The people of Petra used engineering to thrive in a dry environment.
Petra received more rain than other cities in the region.
Most of Petra’s buildings were destroyed by winter storms.
explain: The text focuses on how Petra’s builders worked with the dry landscape, especially their water systems. Nothing says they were the first.

prompt:
Pigeons living in cities often have darker feathers than pigeons in the countryside. Researchers have proposed one possible reason: the pigment that darkens feathers can bind some metals, such as zinc and lead. City pigeons with darker feathers may therefore be able to store some of the metals they pick up from polluted streets in their feathers, which they later shed, instead of in their bodies.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Pigeons in the countryside are healthier than pigeons in cities.
Darker feathers might help city pigeons deal with metal pollution.
Pollution causes pigeons’ feathers to turn darker.
Researchers have proved that zinc is harmless to pigeons.
explain: The text offers a possible reason darker feathers are common in cities: they may help pigeons get rid of metals. It doesn’t say pollution causes the color.

prompt:
Teodor told everyone he hadn’t entered the science fair to win. Still, when the judges finally posted the results, he found reasons to walk past the board three times: once to “fix his shoelace,” once to “get water,” and once without any excuse at all.

Based on the text, what is most likely true about Teodor?
options: He doesn’t know where the results are posted.
He cares about the results more than he admits.
He is certain that he has won.
He has decided not to look at the results.
explain: He claims not to care, yet keeps inventing excuses to check the board, so he cares more than he admits.

prompt:
In 1858, an unusually hot summer made the sewage-filled River Thames smell so bad that Londoners called it the Great Stink. The crisis pushed Parliament to fund a vast network of sewers designed by the engineer Joseph Bazalgette, which carried waste away from the city center. Outbreaks of cholera, a disease spread by contaminated water, became far less common in London after the system was completed.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Joseph Bazalgette was the most famous engineer of the 1800s.
A crisis in 1858 led London to build a sewer system that improved public health.
The summer of 1858 was the hottest ever recorded in London.
Cholera was spread mainly by bad smells.
explain: The text moves from the 1858 crisis to the sewer system it prompted, and then to the health benefits.

prompt:
Some museums are beginning to let visitors handle exact replicas of fragile artifacts. Supporters say touch helps people understand an object’s weight, texture and purpose in a way that looking through glass cannot. Because the replicas can be replaced, museums can offer this experience without risking damage to the originals.

According to the text, why can museums let visitors handle the replicas without much concern?
options: Replicas are more interesting than the originals.
Visitors handle objects more gently than expected.
The originals are stored in other museums.
explain: The text says that “because the replicas can be replaced,” there is no risk to the originals.

prompt:
For years, the composer Mira Halvorsen refused to explain the titles of her pieces, insisting that listeners should bring their own meanings to the music. In a late interview, however, she admitted that each title came from a line in a letter her sister had written to her, though she still declined to say which letters.

Based on the text, which choice best describes Halvorsen’s attitude toward explaining her work in the late interview?
options: She revealed the source of her titles while still keeping some details private.
She regretted ever giving her pieces titles.
She explained the meaning of every one of her titles.
She insisted that the titles had no source at all.
explain: She shared where the titles came from (her sister’s letters) but wouldn’t say which letters, so she revealed some information and kept some private.

prompt:
In a short story, the narrator describes her neighbor, Mr. Okoro, as remarkably patient.

Which quotation from the story most effectively illustrates this claim?
options: “Mr. Okoro’s garden was the greenest on the street.”
“When the delivery truck blocked his driveway for an hour, Mr. Okoro simply sat on his steps and read until it left.”
“Mr. Okoro owned a gray car that he washed every Sunday.”
“Everyone on our street knew Mr. Okoro’s name.”
explain: Calmly reading for an hour while blocked in shows patience. The other quotations describe him but not his patience.

prompt:
Biologist Clara Voss and her team hypothesize that bumblebees prefer flowers that are slightly warmer than the surrounding air, since warm nectar takes less energy for a bee to process.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the team’s hypothesis?
options: Bumblebees visited flowers more often on sunny days than on cloudy days.
When given a choice between otherwise identical artificial flowers, bumblebees visited warmed flowers more often than unwarmed ones.
Bumblebees are able to fly at lower temperatures than many other insects.
Some flowers produce more nectar than others.
explain: Only the artificial-flower test isolates temperature: the flowers are identical except for warmth. Sunny days differ in many ways besides flower temperature.

prompt:
Some ornithologists claim that the bright red feathers of male house finches signal good health to potential mates, since only well-fed, disease-free birds can produce the deepest red color.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken this claim?
options: Male house finches with the brightest red feathers were, on average, no healthier than males with duller feathers.
Female house finches are less brightly colored than males.
House finches eat a variety of seeds and fruits.
The red color of the feathers comes from pigments in the birds’ food.
explain: If color doesn’t track health, it can’t be a reliable signal of health. The finding that the color comes from food is consistent with the claim (well-fed birds get more pigment).

prompt:
In a novel, the narrator, who has just moved from a farm to a large city, finds the city overwhelming.

Which quotation from the novel most effectively illustrates this claim?
options: “I had always wanted to see the ocean.”
“My new apartment had a small window facing east.”
“Horns, voices and engines pressed in from every side until I could hardly hear my own thoughts.”
“The farm had been in my family for three generations.”
explain: Noise pressing in “from every side” until she can’t think is a direct image of being overwhelmed.

prompt:
Historian Dev Raman argues that the opening of a canal in 1825 transformed the economy of the small town of Millbrook.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Raman’s argument?
options: Tax records show that the number of businesses in Millbrook tripled in the ten years after the canal opened, while nearby towns without canal access grew little.
The canal was dug mostly by hand.
Several famous travelers wrote about visiting Millbrook in the 1830s.
explain: A sharp rise in businesses after the canal, with no similar rise in towns without it, ties the economic change to the canal.

prompt:
An ecologist suggests that a decline in a region’s butterfly population was caused mainly by the loss of milkweed, the only plant on which the butterflies lay their eggs.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the ecologist’s suggestion?
options: The butterflies also feed on the nectar of several other flowers.
Milkweed grows quickly in disturbed soil.
Butterfly numbers fell just as sharply in areas where milkweed remained abundant.
Many people plant milkweed in their gardens.
explain: If butterflies declined even where milkweed was plentiful, milkweed loss can’t be the main cause.

prompt:
Psychologists have claimed that students who take lecture notes by hand remember the material better than students who type notes, because writing by hand forces them to summarize rather than copy word for word.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the psychologists’ claim?
options: Students who typed notes wrote down more words than students who wrote by hand.
Most students prefer typing to writing by hand.
Students who handwrote notes on a lecture scored higher on a test about it a week later than students who typed notes on the same lecture.
Laptops are now common in many classrooms.
explain: Better recall a week later for handwriters is direct evidence for the claim. The number of words typed is consistent with the explanation but says nothing about memory.

prompt:
In a memoir, the author suggests that she regretted leaving her hometown as a young woman.

Which quotation from the memoir most effectively illustrates this suggestion?
options: “The train left at six in the morning, and the platform was empty.”
“For years afterward, I found myself mapping my old streets in my head before I fell asleep, wishing I could walk them again.”
“My hometown was known for its apple orchards.”
“I moved to the capital to study engineering.”
explain: Longing to walk her old streets again shows regret. The other quotations give facts about the move without any feeling about it.

prompt:
Most plants make their own food through photosynthesis, using the green pigment chlorophyll to capture energy from sunlight. The ghost pipe, a white plant that grows on dark forest floors, contains no chlorophyll. Therefore, the ghost pipe must \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: get its nutrients in some way other than photosynthesis.
produce more chlorophyll in the summer.
be the only plant without leaves.
explain: Without chlorophyll, it can’t photosynthesize, so it must get nutrients another way. (It actually takes them from fungi in the soil.)

prompt:
Archaeologists excavating an ancient village found hundreds of pottery fragments made from a type of clay that occurs only in a region about 300 kilometers away. They found no kilns, clay deposits or pottery-making tools at the village itself. These findings suggest that the villagers \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: made all of their pottery from local clay.
probably obtained their pottery through trade or travel with that distant region.
never used pottery for storing food.
were the first people to make pottery in the area.
explain: The clay comes from far away and there’s no sign of local pottery-making, so the pottery was probably brought in.

prompt:
In a study, two groups of mice explored a maze once. The next day, one group slept normally, while the other was kept awake for several hours. When placed in the maze again, the mice that had slept found the exit much faster than the mice that had been kept awake. These results suggest that \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: sleep may help mice remember what they have learned.
mice that are kept awake become more curious.
mazes are too difficult for most mice.
mice cannot learn anything after being kept awake.
explain: The only difference between the groups was sleep, and the rested mice did better, so sleep may help memory. “Cannot learn anything” goes too far.

prompt:
A bakery’s owner noticed that her lemon tarts sold out by noon every Saturday but that she often had several left at closing on weekdays. To reduce waste and still satisfy her Saturday customers, she should probably \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: bake more lemon tarts on Saturdays and fewer on weekdays.
raise the price of all her baked goods.
explain: Demand is high on Saturdays and low on weekdays, so matching supply to each day solves both problems.

prompt:
Geologists use layers of rock to date fossils: in undisturbed rock, lower layers are older than the layers above them. At one site, a layer of volcanic ash has been dated to 12,000 years ago. A fossil found in an undisturbed layer directly above the ash must therefore be \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
explain: Higher layers are younger, so a fossil above the 12,000-year-old ash formed after it.

prompt:
Songbirds in noisy cities often sing at higher pitches than members of the same species in quiet forests. Some researchers have suggested that this difference evolved over many generations. But when researchers played recordings of traffic noise in a quiet park, the birds there raised the pitch of their songs within minutes. This finding suggests that \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: birds in quiet forests cannot hear low-pitched songs.
at least some of the pitch difference may result from birds adjusting their songs in the moment, not only from evolution.
traffic noise causes birds to stop singing entirely.
city birds and forest birds belong to different species.
explain: The birds changed pitch within minutes, which is far too fast for evolution, so individual birds can adjust. The text doesn’t rule out evolution entirely, so “not only” is appropriately careful.

prompt:
Some plants form partnerships with soil fungi, which help the plants absorb nutrients in exchange for sugars. In an experiment, plants grown with the fungi grew much larger than plants without them when the soil was poor in nutrients. In nutrient-rich soil, however, plants with and without the fungi grew to about the same size. These results suggest that \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the fungi harm plants growing in rich soil.
the benefit plants get from the fungi depends on how many nutrients the soil already contains.
plants cannot survive without the fungi.
the fungi produce nutrients on their own.
explain: The fungi helped only in poor soil, so their benefit depends on soil nutrients. Equal sizes in rich soil mean the fungi don’t harm plants there.

prompt:
Historians long believed that the earliest surviving map of the island was drawn in 1620, the year the first detailed survey of its coast was completed. Recently, a map of the island was found in a ship captain’s logbook dated 1611. Although it is less detailed than the 1620 map, it correctly shows several bays that the survey later recorded. If the logbook’s date is accurate, it would suggest that \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: at least some of the island’s coastline had been mapped before the 1620 survey.
the ship captain drew the 1620 map.
no one visited the island before 1611.
explain: A 1611 map showing real bays means some mapping happened before 1620. Nothing suggests the survey was wrong or that the captain drew the later map.

prompt:
The museum guard asked visitors not to \_\_\_\_\_\_ the paintings, since oils from their fingers can damage the surface.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: Oils from fingers only matter if visitors **touch** the paintings.

prompt:
Although the forecast called for sunshine, the afternoon turned \_\_\_\_\_\_, and the picnic was moved indoors.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: “Although” signals a contrast with sunshine, and moving the picnic indoors suggests bad weather: **stormy**.

prompt:
The two species of beetle look so \_\_\_\_\_\_ that even experts sometimes need a microscope to tell them apart.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: Needing a microscope to tell them apart means they look **similar**.

prompt:
The new evidence did not \_\_\_\_\_\_ the detective’s theory; instead, it raised doubts about a key part of it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: “Instead, it raised doubts” contrasts with what the evidence didn’t do: it didn’t **confirm** the theory.

prompt:
The author’s tone in the letter is \_\_\_\_\_\_: she thanks the committee warmly but makes clear that she will not change her decision.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: Warm thanks is polite; refusing to change her decision is firm.

prompt:
Over many years, the teacher worked to **cultivate** her students’ curiosity, encouraging them to ask questions about everything they read.

As used in the text, what does the word “cultivate” most nearly mean?
explain: Encouraging questions helps curiosity grow, so “cultivate” means **develop** here, not its farming sense.

prompt:
The new treatment does not cure the disease, but it can **arrest** its progress, keeping symptoms from getting worse for years.

As used in the text, what does the word “arrest” most nearly mean?
explain: Keeping symptoms from getting worse means halting, or **stopping**, the disease’s progress.

prompt:
The scientist’s conclusions were \_\_\_\_\_\_: she noted that the sample was small and that further studies might produce different results.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: Noting a small sample and possible different results means the conclusions are not final: **tentative**.

prompt:
Critics found the film’s plot \_\_\_\_\_\_, noting that nearly every twist could be predicted from the opening scene.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: A plot whose twists are all predictable follows a familiar formula: **formulaic**.

prompt:
Rather than \_\_\_\_\_\_ the rival company’s success, the CEO studied its methods closely and adopted several of them.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: “Rather than” sets up the opposite of studying and adopting the methods: **dismissing** them. Imitating is what the CEO actually did.

prompt:
The axolotl, a salamander found in lakes near Mexico City, can regrow lost legs, parts of its heart, and even parts of its brain. Scientists study the axolotl in the hope of learning how to help human tissues heal.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To describe an unusual ability of the axolotl and explain why scientists study it
To argue that axolotls should be kept as pets
To explain how the lakes near Mexico City formed
To compare axolotls with other kinds of salamanders
explain: The first sentence describes the regrowing ability; the second explains why scientists study it.

prompt:
To make bread, a baker first mixes flour, water, yeast and salt into a dough. Next, the dough rests for several hours as the yeast produces gas that makes it rise. Finally, the baker shapes the loaf and bakes it in a hot oven.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes the steps of a process in order.
It compares two kinds of bread.
It argues that homemade bread is better than store-bought bread.
It explains the history of yeast.
explain: “First… Next… Finally” marks the steps of a process.

prompt:
For years, the old train station sat empty, its windows boarded up. Then a group of local artists asked to use it as a studio. Today, the station holds a gallery, a café and a weekly market that draws visitors from across the region.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes a building’s years of neglect and then its transformation.
It argues that all old train stations should become art galleries.
It compares two different train stations.
It explains how trains are repaired.
explain: The text moves from an empty, boarded-up station to a busy gallery and market.

prompt:
Many people think of bats as dangerous pests. ==In fact, a single little brown bat can eat hundreds of mosquito-sized insects in an hour.== By eating insects that damage crops, bats save farmers large amounts of money each year.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It gives a specific example that challenges the view described in the first sentence.
It explains why bats are considered dangerous.
It describes how mosquitoes spread disease.
It introduces a claim that the final sentence disputes.
explain: “In fact” introduces evidence that bats are useful, which challenges the idea that they are pests.

prompt:
In 1950, about 30 percent of the world’s people lived in cities. By 2018, that share had risen to about 55 percent, and the United Nations projects that it will reach about 68 percent by 2050.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To describe how the share of people living in cities has grown over time
To argue that cities are better places to live than rural areas
To explain why people move to cities
To criticize the United Nations’ projections
explain: The text gives figures for 1950, 2018 and 2050, all showing growth. It never explains why or argues anything.

prompt:
Venice, Italy, is built on more than 100 small islands in a lagoon. ==Instead of streets, many of its neighborhoods are connected by canals, and residents often travel by boat.== Hundreds of bridges also link the islands for people traveling on foot.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes a feature of the city that results from its unusual location.
It argues that Venice should build more roads.
It explains how Venice was founded.
It contradicts the claim made in the first sentence.
explain: Because the city sits on islands in a lagoon, canals take the place of streets.

prompt:
Lena had rehearsed the speech for weeks. She knew every pause, every joke, every place to look up at the audience. ==But when she stepped onto the stage and saw her grandmother in the front row, wiping her eyes, Lena set her notes aside.== She spoke for ten minutes without once thinking about what came next.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It marks a turning point, as Lena abandons her careful preparation in response to an emotional moment.
It explains why Lena had rehearsed for weeks.
It suggests that Lena forgot her speech because she was nervous.
It describes how the audience reacted to the speech.
explain: “But” turns from the weeks of preparation to Lena putting her notes aside after seeing her grandmother.

prompt:
Some critics dismiss video games as a waste of time. Researchers studying surgeons, however, found that those who regularly played video games made fewer errors in a simulated operation using a camera and long instruments than those who did not, perhaps because both activities require precise hand–eye coordination while watching a screen.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To present evidence that playing video games may have a benefit that critics overlook
To argue that surgeons should be required to play video games
To explain how camera-guided surgery is performed
To agree with critics that video games are a waste of time
explain: The study counters the critics with a possible benefit. It doesn’t go so far as to say surgeons must play games.

prompt:
Early astronomers placed Earth at the center of the universe. In the 1500s, Copernicus proposed instead that Earth and the other planets orbit the Sun. His model was not quickly accepted, but telescope observations in the following century, such as Galileo’s discovery of moons orbiting Jupiter, provided support for it.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes an older view, presents a challenge to that view, and explains how the challenge gained support.
It presents a theory and then explains why it was proven wrong.
It describes Galileo’s life in detail.
It compares several modern theories about the universe.
explain: Old view (Earth-centered) → challenge (Copernicus) → support (telescope observations).

prompt:
Critics of rent control argue that capping rents discourages landlords from maintaining their buildings. A study of one city found that this did happen in some cases. But the same study found that rent control allowed long-term tenants to stay in their neighborhoods, preserving communities that might otherwise have broken apart.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To present evidence that rent control has both drawbacks and benefits
To argue that rent control should be abolished
To explain how landlords set rents
To show that critics of rent control are entirely wrong
explain: The study confirms the critics’ concern in some cases but also finds a benefit: both sides.

prompt:
**Text 1**
Many people believe that goldfish can remember things for only about three seconds.

**Text 2**
In experiments, goldfish have learned to push a lever to get food, and they remembered how to do it months later.

Based on the texts, how would the researchers in Text 2 most likely respond to the belief described in Text 1?
options: By saying the belief is mistaken, since goldfish can remember things for months
By agreeing that goldfish forget everything after three seconds
By saying that goldfish can remember only the color of their food
By arguing that goldfish are unable to learn
explain: Remembering a skill for months directly contradicts a three-second memory.

prompt:
**Text 1**
Many gardeners pull dandelions from their lawns, treating them as weeds with no value.

**Text 2**
Dandelions bloom early in spring, when few other flowers are open, and they provide an important source of food for bees coming out of winter.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the gardeners described in Text 1?
options: By suggesting that dandelions have a value the gardeners may overlook
By agreeing that dandelions should be removed from every lawn
By arguing that bees damage lawns
By claiming that dandelions bloom only in the fall
explain: Text 2 points out that dandelions feed bees, a value the gardeners in Text 1 ignore.

prompt:
**Text 1**
Self-driving cars will make roads safer, because most crashes are caused by human error.

**Text 2**
Most crashes do involve human error. But self-driving systems can make different kinds of mistakes, such as misreading unusual road signs or failing in heavy snow. Whether these cars make roads safer overall depends on how often such new errors occur.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that human error causes most crashes but noting that self-driving cars might introduce new kinds of errors
By arguing that self-driving cars will never be allowed on public roads
By denying that human error causes most crashes
By agreeing completely that self-driving cars will make roads safer
explain: Text 2 accepts the premise (human error) but adds a condition: the new errors must be rare.

prompt:
**Text 1**
Standardized tests are the fairest way to compare students from different schools, because every student answers the same questions under the same conditions.

**Text 2**
Identical questions do not guarantee equal conditions. Students whose families can afford tutoring and practice materials often arrive better prepared, so test scores may partly reflect family income rather than ability alone.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the argument in Text 1?
options: By arguing that giving everyone the same questions does not make the comparison fully fair, since students have unequal access to preparation
By agreeing that standardized tests are perfectly fair
By claiming that standardized tests should include more questions
By arguing that tutoring has no effect on test scores
explain: Text 2 attacks the idea that “the same conditions” exist, pointing to unequal preparation.

prompt:
**Text 1**
A novelist says she outlines every chapter before she begins writing, because a detailed plan keeps her from losing her way.

**Text 2**
Another novelist says she never outlines. She discovers the story by writing it, and a plan would take away the surprise that keeps her interested.

Which choice best describes a difference in how the two novelists view planning?
options: The first sees planning as a way to stay on course, while the second sees it as removing the discovery that motivates her.
Both believe outlines are essential to good writing.
The first thinks planning makes writing less interesting.
The second outlines only the final chapter of each book.
explain: Novelist 1: plans keep her on track. Novelist 2: plans would kill the surprise.

prompt:
**Text 1**
Neanderthals, who lived in Europe and western Asia until about 40,000 years ago, have often been portrayed as less intelligent than early modern humans and unable to create art or symbols.

**Text 2**
Recent discoveries challenge this view. Markings in caves in Spain have been dated to more than 64,000 years ago, before modern humans arrived in Europe, suggesting that Neanderthals made them. Some researchers, however, question whether the dating method is reliable.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely describe the view presented in Text 1?
options: As being challenged by new evidence, although that evidence is itself debated
As fully supported by the cave markings
As unrelated to the study of Neanderthals
explain: Text 2 says the discoveries challenge the view, then notes doubts about the dating, so “completely disproven” goes too far.

prompt:
**Text 1**
An economist argues that tipping should be replaced with fixed wages for restaurant servers, because tips depend more on customers’ moods than on the quality of service.

**Text 2**
A study of restaurant customers found that the size of their tips was only weakly related to how they rated their service. Factors such as the weather and the size of the bill predicted tips nearly as well.

How would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the economist’s claim that tips depend on things other than service quality?
options: By presenting findings that are consistent with the claim
By arguing that tips closely reflect the quality of service
By claiming that the weather has no effect on tipping
By recommending that servers be paid only in tips
explain: A weak link between service ratings and tips, with weather mattering, supports the economist’s point.

prompt:
**Text 1**
Some historians argue that the decline of many ancient Maya cities in the 800s was caused mainly by a series of severe droughts, citing evidence from lake sediments.

**Text 2**
Drought probably played a role. But the cities did not all decline at once, and some cities in dry areas lasted longer than cities in wetter ones. Warfare and political conflict among cities, other historians argue, must also have been important.

Based on the texts, how would the historians in Text 2 most likely respond to the argument in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that drought contributed but arguing that it cannot fully explain the pattern of decline
By denying that any droughts occurred in the region
By agreeing that drought alone caused the decline
By arguing that lake sediments cannot provide evidence about past climates
explain: “Drought probably played a role. But…” accepts part of Text 1 and then points to evidence that drought alone can’t explain.

prompt:
Arctic terns migrate farther than any other animal, flying from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back every year. Over its lifetime, a single tern may fly a distance equal to about three round trips to the Moon.

According to the text, what is true about Arctic terns?
options: They travel extremely long distances during their lives.
They live in the Antarctic all year.
They migrate only once in their lives.
explain: The text says they migrate between the poles every year, covering huge distances.

prompt:
Mangrove trees grow along tropical coastlines, where their tangled roots hold soil in place. During storms, these roots slow incoming waves, protecting coastal villages from flooding and erosion.

According to the text, how do mangroves protect coastal villages?
options: Their roots slow waves during storms and hold the soil in place.
They provide wood for building sea walls.
explain: The text names two ways: roots hold soil and slow incoming waves.

prompt:
The Dead Sea is so salty that swimmers float easily on its surface. The salt also makes it impossible for fish and most other living things to survive there, which is how the lake got its name.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The Dead Sea’s extreme saltiness affects both swimmers and wildlife.
Swimming in the Dead Sea is dangerous.
Fish are the only animals that cannot live in the Dead Sea.
The Dead Sea is the largest lake in the world.
explain: Both sentences describe effects of the salt: floating swimmers and almost no life.

prompt:
Every evening, Mrs. Patel set two cups on the table, though she had lived alone for years. She filled only one with tea, and sometimes, while she drank, she glanced at the empty chair across from her and smiled.

Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about Mrs. Patel?
options: She is remembering someone who used to share tea with her.
She is expecting a guest who is late.
She dislikes drinking tea and plans to stop.
She sets out two cups by accident.
explain: She has lived alone for years yet still sets a second cup and smiles at the empty chair: a fond memory.

prompt:
For a long time, scientists thought that the human brain stopped producing new neurons after childhood. Studies in the 1990s, however, found evidence that new neurons continue to form in certain parts of the adult brain, such as the hippocampus, an area important for memory.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Research has challenged the belief that the brain stops producing new neurons after childhood.
The hippocampus is the only part of the brain that matters for memory.
Children’s brains produce more neurons than adult brains do.
Scientists in the 1990s proved that adults cannot form new memories.
explain: The text sets up an old belief and then the evidence against it.

prompt:
Ancient Polynesian navigators sailed thousands of kilometers across the Pacific without maps or instruments. They read the positions of stars, the shapes of ocean swells and the flight paths of seabirds to find islands that might be days away.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Polynesian navigators used natural signs to travel long distances across the ocean.
Polynesian navigators were the first to draw maps of the Pacific.
Seabirds were the only guide Polynesian navigators used.
Polynesian voyages were usually short trips between nearby islands.
explain: The text describes how they crossed long distances using stars, swells and birds.

prompt:
Although the inventor received hundreds of patents during his life, he kept a notebook he called his “book of failures,” in which he recorded every experiment that did not work. He told his assistants that the notebook was the most valuable thing in his laboratory.

Based on the text, what is most strongly suggested about the inventor?
options: He believed that unsuccessful experiments provided valuable information.
He was ashamed of his failures and hid the notebook.
Most of his experiments were successful.
His assistants wrote the notebook for him.
explain: Calling the record of failures his most valuable possession shows he learned from them.

prompt:
Many people assume that more parking will draw more shoppers downtown. But when one city removed parking spaces along its main street to widen the sidewalks and add outdoor seating, sales at nearby shops rose. Shoppers, it seems, may value a pleasant place to walk more than a convenient place to park.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Making a downtown more pleasant for walking may help businesses more than adding parking.
Cities should remove all parking from their downtowns.
Most shoppers walk to downtown stores.
explain: The example and the last sentence point to one idea: walkability may matter more than parking. “All parking” goes too far.

prompt:
The professor paused at the door of the lecture hall, as she had every Monday for thirty years, and looked out at the rows of seats. Today they were empty; the semester had ended, and so had her career. She straightened a chair in the front row, turned off the lights and closed the door gently behind her.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A professor marks the end of her long career with a quiet, familiar ritual.
A professor is upset that no students came to her lecture.
A professor is preparing for the start of a new semester.
A professor complains about the condition of the lecture hall.
explain: Her career has ended, and she repeats her usual pause at the door, gently, one last time.

prompt:
Nearly all bananas sold in stores are one variety, the Cavendish. New plants are grown from cuttings rather than seeds, so the plants are almost genetically identical. A fungal disease that kills Cavendish plants has now spread to banana farms on several continents.

Based on the text, what is most strongly suggested?
options: A single disease could threaten much of the world’s supply of store-bought bananas.
Bananas grown from seeds taste better than those grown from cuttings.
The Cavendish banana is immune to most diseases.
Banana farms are found on only one continent.
explain: Genetically identical plants share the same weakness, and the disease is spreading widely.

prompt:
In a poem, the speaker describes the ocean as powerful.

Which quotation from the poem most effectively illustrates this claim?
options: “Its waves pound the cliffs until the stones themselves give way.”
“The water shimmers green beneath the dock.”
“A gull drifts lazily above the harbor.”
“Children build castles in the damp sand.”
explain: Waves breaking stone shows power; the others describe calm scenes.

prompt:
A student claims that her town’s new recycling program has been successful.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the student’s claim?
options: In the program’s first year, the amount of material recycled in the town doubled.
The town’s recycling bins are painted blue.
Some residents said they had not heard of the program.
explain: Doubling the amount recycled is a direct measure of success.

prompt:
A biologist claims that some species of ants farm fungus for food.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the biologist’s claim?
options: Leafcutter ants carry pieces of leaves into their nests, where they use them to grow a fungus that the colony eats.
Leafcutter ants can carry leaves many times their own weight.
Some ant colonies contain millions of ants.
Fungi grow best in damp, dark places.
explain: Growing a fungus and then eating it is farming fungus for food.

prompt:
A store manager claims that playing slow music causes customers to spend more money.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the manager’s claim?
options: On days when the store played slow music, customers spent the same amount on average as on days when it played fast music.
Customers said they liked the slow music.
The store is busiest on weekends.
On days with slow music, customers stayed longer and spent more.
explain: If spending is the same either way, the music isn’t changing it. The option saying customers spent more on slow-music days would support the claim, not weaken it.

prompt:
In a novel, the narrator suggests that her brother is stubborn.

Which quotation from the novel most effectively illustrates this claim?
options: “Once Marco decided something, no argument in the world could move him, not even proof that he was wrong.”
“Marco was two years older than me and much taller.”
“Marco loved to fix old radios in the garage.”
“Marco often laughed at his own jokes.”
explain: Refusing to change his mind even in the face of proof is stubbornness.

prompt:
A researcher hypothesizes that learning a musical instrument improves children’s attention skills, and that the improvement is caused by the music training itself rather than by other differences between children.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researcher’s hypothesis?
options: Children randomly assigned to take music lessons for a year improved more on attention tests than children randomly assigned to take art lessons.
Children who chose to take music lessons scored higher on attention tests than children who did not.
Many children enjoy playing musical instruments.
Attention skills usually improve as children get older.
explain: Random assignment rules out other differences between children. Kids who **chose** music might already have been more attentive.

prompt:
Researchers claim that a certain bird species finds its way during migration by sensing Earth’s magnetic field.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the researchers’ claim?
options: Birds of the species fitted with small magnets that disrupt their magnetic sense still flew in the correct direction.
The species migrates mostly at night.
Many bird species can detect Earth’s magnetic field.
The species flies more than 3,000 kilometers each year.
explain: If birds navigate fine with their magnetic sense disrupted, they must not depend on it.

prompt:
In a play, a character expresses both admiration and envy toward her sister.

Which quotation from the play most effectively illustrates this claim?
options: “Everything she touches turns to success, and I am proud of her, truly, though some nights I wish the world had been half as kind to me.”
“My sister and I grew up in the same small house.”
“I am so proud of my sister’s success.”
“I wish the world had been kinder to me.”
explain: The claim has two parts. Only the quotation that pairs “I am proud of her” with wishing the world had been as kind to her shows both admiration and envy.

prompt:
Economists claim that a city’s new tax on sugary drinks reduced how many of those drinks people bought.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the economists’ claim?
options: Sales of sugary drinks in the city fell by about a third in the year after the tax began, while sales in nearby cities without the tax stayed about the same.
Sales of sugary drinks in the city fell after the tax began, and they also fell by the same amount in nearby cities without the tax.
Many residents said they disliked the tax.
The tax raised money for the city’s parks.
explain: A drop only where the tax applied points to the tax. If sales fell everywhere, something else could explain it.

prompt:
A paleontologist claims that a certain dinosaur species was a fast runner, pointing to its long, slender leg bones.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the paleontologist’s claim?
options: Analysis of the leg bones shows that the muscles attached in a way that would have made rapid movement difficult.
Other dinosaurs with long leg bones are thought to have been fast.
The species lived on open plains.
Fossils of the species have been found on three continents.
explain: If the muscle attachments made speed difficult, the long bones don’t mean it was fast.

prompt:
Plants on a sunny windowsill often lean toward the glass. This happens because cells on the shaded side of the stem grow faster than cells on the sunny side. As a result, \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the stem bends toward the light.
the leaves turn away from the window.
explain: If the shaded side grows longer, the stem curves toward the sunny side.

prompt:
A library found that its e-book loans doubled during a month when its building was closed for repairs, while total borrowing stayed about the same. This suggests that \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: many patrons switched to e-books when they could not visit the building.
patrons stopped reading during the repairs.
the library bought fewer e-books that month.
e-books are always more popular than printed books.
explain: Total borrowing held steady while e-books doubled, so readers moved from print to e-books.

prompt:
Some lizards can detach their tails when grabbed by a predator. The detached tail keeps wriggling for several minutes. This most likely helps the lizard by \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: distracting the predator while the lizard escapes.
explain: A moving tail holds the predator’s attention while the lizard gets away.

prompt:
In a study, people viewed the same painting with one of two labels. Half were told it was by a famous artist, and half were told it was by an unknown student. Those told it was by the famous artist rated it as more beautiful. This suggests that \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: people’s judgments of art can be influenced by what they believe about who made it.
famous artists always produce better paintings.
the painting was actually made by a student.
people cannot tell one painting from another.
explain: The painting was identical; only the label changed, and it changed the ratings.

prompt:
Fennec foxes, which live in hot deserts, have very large ears. Blood flowing through the thin skin of the ears releases heat into the air. Arctic foxes, in contrast, have small, rounded ears. This difference suggests that \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: ear size in foxes may be related to how much body heat the animals need to release or keep.
arctic foxes have better hearing than fennec foxes.
fennec foxes are larger than arctic foxes.
all desert animals have large ears.
explain: Large ears release heat (useful in deserts); small ears would keep heat in (useful in the Arctic). “All desert animals” goes too far.

prompt:
Historians note that during the war, soldiers’ letters home were often read by officers before being mailed, and that soldiers knew this. When reading these letters today, historians should therefore keep in mind that \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: soldiers may have left out details or feelings they did not want officers to see.
the letters were written by officers.
the letters contain no useful information.
explain: Knowing officers would read them, soldiers may have held things back.

prompt:
Archaeologists found wheat seeds at a site 9,000 years old. Wild wheat drops its seeds as soon as they ripen, but this wheat held on to its seeds until harvest, a trait that develops only when people repeatedly plant seeds gathered from plants that kept their seeds. The find therefore suggests that \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: people at the site were already farming wheat 9,000 years ago.
wild wheat did not grow near the site.
the site was abandoned before wheat was harvested.
wheat seeds cannot survive for 9,000 years.
explain: The trait comes only from repeated planting by people, so they must have been farming.

prompt:
Two groups of students studied the same chapter. One group reread it twice; the other read it once and then took a practice quiz. A week later, the quiz group remembered more, even though the rereading group had predicted they would do better. These results suggest that \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: students may not always be able to judge which study methods will help them most.
rereading a chapter twice is the most effective way to study.
students who take practice quizzes study less overall.
students forget everything they read within a week.
explain: The rereading group expected to do better and didn’t, so their sense of what works was wrong.

prompt:
Bus ridership in a town fell by 20 percent in the year after fares went up. During the same year, however, the town’s largest employer moved its offices to a city 50 kilometers away. It is therefore possible that the fare increase \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: was not the only cause of the drop in ridership.
was the only reason fewer people rode the bus.
increased the number of people riding the bus.
explain: “However” introduces another possible cause, so the fare increase may not explain everything.

prompt:
A garden spider rebuilds its web every night, eating the old silk before spinning a new web. Researchers found that spider silk contains a large amount of protein, which takes energy to produce. Eating the old web most likely helps the spider \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: recover some of the protein and energy used to make the silk.
hide from predators during the day.
catch insects that were stuck in the old web.
make its new web a different shape.
explain: Silk is costly protein; eating it lets the spider reuse those materials.

prompt:
The marathon route passes several famous \_\_\_\_\_\_ including the old city hall and the cathedral.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: “Including…” is a phrase, not a sentence, so a comma attaches it. A semicolon or period would leave it stranded.

prompt:
Ostriches cannot \_\_\_\_\_\_ they can run at about 70 kilometers per hour.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: A comma plus “but” joins two complete sentences. No comma goes after “but”.

prompt:
Although the storm had passed by \_\_\_\_\_\_ the roads stayed closed for most of the day.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: An opening “Although…” clause is followed by a comma.

prompt:
Many spices that are now common in European kitchens, such as pepper and \_\_\_\_\_\_ were once so valuable that they were traded like gold.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The “such as” phrase opens with a comma, so it must close with one before “were”.

prompt:
The scientist’s goal was \_\_\_\_\_\_ to find a way to store solar energy cheaply enough for every home.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: “The scientist’s goal was simple” is complete, and what follows explains the goal, so a colon fits.

prompt:
Mount \_\_\_\_\_\_ last erupted in 1707, is Japan’s highest mountain.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The “which” clause is extra information, closed by the comma after 1707, so it needs an opening comma too.

prompt:
In 1953, Rosalind Franklin’s X-ray images helped scientists work out the structure of \_\_\_\_\_\_ the molecule that carries genetic information.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: “The molecule that carries…” renames DNA, so a comma sets it off. A semicolon needs a complete sentence after it.

prompt:
The study had an unexpected \_\_\_\_\_\_ participants who slept less said they felt more creative, though their scores on creativity tests were lower.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: A complete sentence comes first, and what follows explains the result, so a colon fits. A comma alone would be a comma splice.

prompt:
Some of the world’s oldest living trees are bristlecone \_\_\_\_\_\_ in California, one of them is more than 4,800 years old.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: Both parts are complete sentences, so a semicolon is needed. “In California” belongs to the second sentence.

prompt:
Researchers who study animal \_\_\_\_\_\_ the ways animals share information with one another—have found that prairie dogs use different alarm calls for different predators.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The explanation ends with a dash before “have”, so it must begin with one.

prompt:
The puppies at the shelter \_\_\_\_\_\_ eager to meet visitors.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The subject is “puppies” (plural), so “are”.

prompt:
Yesterday, the school choir \_\_\_\_\_\_ its final performance of the season.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: “Yesterday” calls for the past tense: “gave”.

prompt:
When archaeologists opened the tomb in 1922, they \_\_\_\_\_\_ objects that had not been seen for more than 3,000 years.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The event happened in 1922, so the simple past “found” matches “opened”.

prompt:
The company announced that \_\_\_\_\_\_ will open a new store downtown next spring.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: A company is a single thing, so the SAT expects “it”.

prompt:
After the muddy game, all eleven \_\_\_\_\_\_ uniforms had to be washed twice.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The uniforms belong to eleven players (plural), so the apostrophe goes after the s: “players’”.

prompt:
One of the most popular exhibits at the science center \_\_\_\_\_\_ a giant model of the human heart that visitors can walk through.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The subject is “one”, not “exhibits”, so “is”.

prompt:
Walking along the beach at sunrise, \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the photographer spotted a pod of dolphins.
a pod of dolphins was spotted by the photographer.
the dolphins were spotted swimming offshore.
there was a pod of dolphins offshore.
explain: The person walking is the photographer, so “the photographer” must come right after the comma.

prompt:
A honeybee beats \_\_\_\_\_\_ wings more than 200 times per second, producing its familiar buzz.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The wings belong to one bee: “its”. “It’s” means “it is”.

prompt:
The museum’s collection of fossils, along with several rare meteorites, \_\_\_\_\_\_ been moved to a new building.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The subject is “collection” (singular). “Along with…” is extra information and doesn’t make the subject plural.

prompt:
The volunteers spent the weekend clearing trails, planting trees, and \_\_\_\_\_\_

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explain: The list items must match: “clearing… planting… repairing”.

prompt:
The library’s old computers were slow and unreliable. \_\_\_\_\_\_ the library replaced them with new ones last month.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: The replacement was caused by the problems: cause and effect.

prompt:
Some dinosaurs were enormous. \_\_\_\_\_\_ *Argentinosaurus* may have weighed more than 70 metric tons.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: *Argentinosaurus* is an example of an enormous dinosaur.

prompt:
First, the students collected water samples from the river. \_\_\_\_\_\_ they tested each sample for bacteria in the school laboratory.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: The second step follows the first: a sequence.

prompt:
Tomatoes need plenty of direct sunlight. \_\_\_\_\_\_ lettuce can grow well in partial shade.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: The two plants have opposite needs: a contrast.

prompt:
Many people assume that sharks are solitary hunters. \_\_\_\_\_\_ some species show complex social behavior, returning to the same companions over many years.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: Social behavior contradicts the assumption that sharks are solitary.

prompt:
Solar panels produce no emissions while generating electricity. \_\_\_\_\_\_ they generate electricity only when the sun is shining, so they must be paired with batteries or other sources.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: The second sentence gives a drawback that qualifies the first: “Still”.

prompt:
The author’s first novel received little attention when it was published. \_\_\_\_\_\_ it is now taught in literature courses around the world.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: The novel’s later success contrasts with how it was first received, and it happens at a later time.

prompt:
Most substances shrink as they freeze. Water, \_\_\_\_\_\_ expands when it freezes, which is why ice floats.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: Water does the opposite of most substances: a contrast.

prompt:
The study found that students who slept at least eight hours did better on memory tests. \_\_\_\_\_\_ the study did not show that more sleep caused the improvement; students who sleep more may differ in other ways.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: The second sentence adds a limitation to the finding: “That said”.

prompt:
Researchers expected the new drug to lower blood pressure, and it did. \_\_\_\_\_\_ it also seemed to improve patients’ sleep, an effect that no one had predicted.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explain: No one predicted the sleep effect, so “Surprisingly” fits. “Instead” would mean blood pressure didn’t fall.

prompt:
The library asked visitors to speak \_\_\_\_\_\_ so that others could read without being disturbed.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: Not disturbing readers means speaking **quietly**.

prompt:
Because the soup was too \_\_\_\_\_\_ to eat, Leo waited a few minutes for it to cool.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: Waiting for soup to cool means it was too **hot**.

prompt:
The mountain path was so \_\_\_\_\_\_ that the hikers had to walk in single file.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: Walking in single file is necessary on a **narrow** path.

prompt:
The scientist’s talk was highly \_\_\_\_\_\_: she explained each idea with everyday examples, and no one in the audience left confused.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: Everyday examples that leave no one confused make the talk easy to understand: **accessible**.

prompt:
Although the new law was meant to help small farms, its effects were \_\_\_\_\_\_: some farms benefited, while others lost money.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: Some farms gained and others lost, so the effects were **mixed**.

prompt:
The two reports \_\_\_\_\_\_ on most points but disagree about how much the project will cost.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: “But disagree about cost” contrasts with what the reports do on most points: **agree**.

prompt:
The team’s early success **fueled** hopes that it might win the championship.

As used in the text, what does the word “fueled” most nearly mean?
explain: Early wins made hopes grow, so “fueled” means **strengthened**.

prompt:
The museum’s new director has a **clear** vision for the collection: every exhibit should connect art to everyday life.

As used in the text, what does the word “clear” most nearly mean?
explain: Her vision is specific and firmly stated, so “clear” means **definite**.

prompt:
The diplomat’s statement was carefully \_\_\_\_\_\_, offering sympathy to both countries without assigning blame to either.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: Treating both sides equally and blaming neither is **impartial**.

prompt:
Early reviews of the novel were \_\_\_\_\_\_, but over the following decades, critics came to regard it as a masterpiece.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: “But” contrasts early reviews with later praise, so the early reviews were negative: **dismissive**.

prompt:
The chemist’s method, though \_\_\_\_\_\_, produced remarkably pure samples: each step took several days, and the whole process required weeks of careful work.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: Weeks of careful, slow work describe a method that is **laborious**.

prompt:
Rather than \_\_\_\_\_\_ the scandal, the company’s new leaders addressed it openly, publishing a full report on what had gone wrong.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: “Rather than” sets up the opposite of addressing it openly: **concealing** it.

prompt:
The researcher cautioned that the link between the two variables was \_\_\_\_\_\_: it appeared in some samples but vanished in others, suggesting that it might be due to chance.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: A link that appears only sometimes and might be chance is weak: **tenuous**.

prompt:
Though the senator **entertained** the proposal for several weeks, she ultimately voted against it.

As used in the text, what does the word “entertained” most nearly mean?
explain: She thought about the proposal before rejecting it, so “entertained” means **considered**.

prompt:
The poet’s later work is marked by \_\_\_\_\_\_: where her early poems used elaborate imagery, her later ones rely on a few plain words.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explain: Moving from elaborate imagery to a few plain words is a move toward severe simplicity: **austerity**.

prompt:
Sunflowers are not just beautiful; they are also useful. Their seeds are eaten by people and birds, and oil pressed from the seeds is used for cooking.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To describe some of the ways sunflowers are useful
To explain how sunflowers turn toward the sun
To argue that birds should not eat sunflower seeds
To compare sunflowers with other flowers
explain: After saying sunflowers are useful, the text lists how: food for people and birds, and cooking oil.

prompt:
Some people think bats are blind, but that is not true. Most bats can see, and many also use echolocation, making sounds and listening for the echoes to find their way in the dark.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It presents a common belief and then corrects it.
It describes a problem and then explains its solution.
